title: Who’s Capturing Value ⛳,Earning Yield 💸, Tokenized Stocks Battleground🥷
teaser: Mega-firms accuse DeFi schemes of running $397M Ponzi operations, while tokenized stocks battlegrounds signal a shift toward centralized players.
summary:
Crypto markets are navigating rapid legal scrutiny alongside structural shifts. The CFTC and SEC jointly filed civil suits against Goliath Ventures Inc., alleging a massive $397 million Ponzi scheme that misdirected funds for staff commissions and payouts. Separately, FlightAware dismissed its lawsuit against Kalshi, signaling potential private settlements amid intense regulatory attention on crypto platforms.

In structural analysis, the battleground is shifting towards tokenized assets. Tokenized equities grew 6.5x since January 2025, with the Linked Security structure dominating. However, experts note a significant valuation gap, suggesting centralized players (like major exchanges/brokers) are far more valuable than pure on-chain protocols due to their proximity to end users.

Meanwhile, large financial institutions accelerated tokenization entry (DTCC, Nasdaq), confirming traditional market infrastructure's growing role in capturing value.
author: TLDR Crypto
content: FlightAware drops lawsuit against Kalshi one day after filing (2 minute read) FlightAware voluntarily dismissed its suit against Kalshi over alleged unauthorized data/trademark use in flight-cancellation markets just one day after filing. Kalshi simultaneously changed its market language from "verified from FlightAware" to "verified from Primary Source Agency," suggesting the parties settled privately. Kalshi still faces active suits and injunctions in New York, Washington, and Michigan over sports-event contracts. CFTC Sues Goliath Ventures Over Alleged $397M DeFi Liquidity Pool Ponzi (3 minute read) The CFTC and SEC filed simultaneous civil suits against Goliath Ventures Inc. and CEO Christopher Delgado, alleging a $397 million Ponzi scheme from November 2022 through February 2026 in which approximately 1,600 customers were told their BTC and ETH would earn 36% annual yields in DEX liquidity pools. Goliath issued fabricated account statements while directing no capital to any DeFi protocol, funneling $174 million to staff as recruiting commissions, $87 million in Ponzi payments to existing customers, and $48 million to Delgado personally for luxury real estate, vehicles, and jewelry. Delgado pleaded guilty in June to wire fraud conspiracy and money laundering charges, and a bankruptcy receiver was appointed in March. The same-day CFTC-SEC filing demonstrates both agencies asserting parallel jurisdiction over crypto fraud, with CFTC Chairman Michael Selig citing an aggressive mandate to police crypto asset markets. Pudgy Penguins Co-Founder Launches NFT Mint on Robinhood Chain (2 minute read) Cole Villemain, removed from Pudgy Penguins in January 2022 amid treasury misuse allegations and scrutinized by ZachXBT, sold out a 44,444-piece NFT collection called Spritehood on Robinhood Chain in 57 minutes on August 11, generating $1.28M (684.28 ETH) across two tiers priced at $17 and $117. The Spritehood smart contract remains unverified on Robinhood Chain's Blockscout explorer, preventing buyers from auditing token mechanics and distribution terms. Villemain has promised future "infrastructure and mechanisms" without publishing verified contract code, and community observers have labeled the project a cash grab with unresolved questions about viability on the chain. Neutrl: Yield Without a Cycle (5 minute read) Crypto-native carry strategies face a structural timing mismatch: funding rates and basis spreads are royalties on speculative activity, so delta-neutral books earn worst when stablecoin demand peaks, a dynamic visible in H1 2026 when top-30 altcoin perpetual volume fell 30%, from $8.4B to $5.9B daily. Neutrl sidesteps this by buying private company locked shares at a 15% discount to the reference price and shorting the equity perpetual referencing the same name, hedging directional exposure from day one. Funding on the short leg averaged 10.9% annualized over a late-May to mid-July window, delivering roughly 20.5 points of total return over a six-month hold. How to Turn $HYPE Funding Rates into Profit (3 minute read) Boros protocol lets traders isolate and trade funding rates as a standalone asset through Yield Units (YU), instruments that pay a fixed rate against the floating funding of a specific perpetual venue. A 4.03pp gap currently exists between HYPE's fixed rate on Hyperliquid (7.93%) and Bybit (3.89%), representing a spread that locks in at trade open and resolves over a 17-day window. The four-leg structure shorts YU on the Hyperliquid market and longs YU on Bybit, then offsets each leg with an opposing HYPE perpetual on the respective exchange, canceling both floating funding obligations and directional price exposure. The remaining return is the fixed rate differential, scaling to 40.30% APR at 10x leverage with no HYPE price risk. $FIGR: The Market May Be Underwriting the Wrong Business (8 minute read) Figure has transitioned from balance-sheet lender to capital-light marketplace operator on Provenance blockchain rails: partner-originated loans reached 78% of Q1 2026 volume, Figure Connect grew from $8M to $1.6B in seven quarters, and ecosystem/technology fees expanded from 5% to 28% of revenue. The pending Kiavi acquisition adds $7B in annual residential transition loan origination at roughly 40% EBITDA margins, volume that should route through the same infrastructure without requiring additional capital deployment. Despite 91% incremental EBITDA margins in 2025 and adjusted EBITDA expanding from negative 4% to 49%, FIGR trades at roughly 12x EBITDA, in line with specialty lenders rather than the Tradeweb/ICE comps the business now resembles. Thin sell-side coverage and FIGR's legacy classification as a crypto proxy have left the market pricing the old balance-sheet model rather than the fee-generating marketplace. Who actually captures value in crypto (5 minute read) Analysis estimates on-chain protocol revenue at roughly $8 billion in 2025 versus roughly $70 billion (range $60-100B) for off-chain/centralized crypto companies (Coinbase, Tether, Binance, Robinhood's crypto arm, etc.), an 8.5x gap. Applying generous multiples, that implies on-chain's entire addressable market cap is about $168 billion versus roughly $840 billion for centralized players, meaning the whole centralized crypto industry is worth about as much as a single AI lab like OpenAI or Anthropic. On-chain revenue is dominated by L1/L2 chains (~49%). Off-chain is dominated by exchanges/brokers (~66%) and stablecoin issuers (~19%). Centralized players win by sitting closer to end users and abstracting away crypto's complexity. Tokenized Stocks: The Next Battleground (8 minute read) Tokenized equities reached ~$1.9B in market size, a 6.5x increase since January 2025, while the tokenized Treasury market stagnated at $15B after April 2026. The SEC's January 2026 taxonomy established four structural models. The Linked Security structure (DeFi-composable, no voting rights, unavailable to US investors) has captured the most share, with Ondo at 45.9% ($851M across 406 equities) and xStocks at 26% ($482M across 183 equities), both operating via Jersey-regulated SPVs. Traditional market infrastructure accelerated entry in mid-2026: DTCC began limited QQQ/SPY tokenization on July 15 after an SEC no-action letter, Nasdaq secured rule-change approval in March 2026 and is building a permissionless gateway with Kraken parent Payward, and NYSE filed its own rule change while signing an MOU with Securitize. Coinbase announced a 1:1 stock-backed token product for non-US customers with onchain usability but has not yet launched.

title: Figma MCP Upgrade 🎨, WhatsApp New Search💬, Claude Watermarks AI 💧
teaser: Tech platforms are grappling with AI integration: Figma links tools to ChatGPT, Anthropic adds invisible watermarks, and Google pauses deepfake satellite images.
summary:
Major tech platforms are integrating advanced capabilities and responding to ethical concerns. These developments underscore a broader industry shift: while AI democratizes idea generation, human expertise is increasingly valued in judgment, selection, and high-level strategic thinking (the concept of 'taste').
author: TLDR Design
content: Figma MCP: Run Weave Tools, Right from Your Favorite Agent (1 minute read) Figma Weave tools can now be run from external AI clients like ChatGPT, Claude, and Cursor through the Figma MCP server. Users can describe a task, such as running a Brand mockup tool, and the agent finds it, executes it, and returns results directly in the conversation. This lets users stay within their chat workflow while preserving context like prompts, images, and brand guidelines. Instead of opening the chat info screen to access search, users would be able to start searching directly from the conversation, with the button appearing when scrolling through older messages. The change streamlines a common task and reflects WhatsApp's ongoing efforts to reduce friction in everyday interactions. Anthropic to Start Watermarking Claude-Generated Text, Images (2 minute read) Anthropic will embed an invisible watermark in text and images generated by Claude, aligning it with the EU AI Act's voluntary Code of Practice. Text watermarking applies to Claude models released after August 2nd, and the mark persists when text is copied to other applications or edited. Images will be marked using C2PA metadata, though detection may fail on short or heavily edited text snippets. Taste is All That's Left (16 minute read) With AI collapsing the distance between idea and working artifact, the friction that once rationed output and trained judgment has disappeared. Taste, the wordless verdict on what is worth keeping, is the one part of the work machines cannot perform. The scarce act is no longer making but choosing what deserves to exist. Is there a retirement crisis in the creative industry? (5 minute read) Many senior creatives are considering early retirement due to economic uncertainty, shrinking margins, and concerns about AI reducing demand for production-focused creative work. However, retirement is not a guaranteed solution and human expertise remains valuable in areas such as strategy, branding, problem-solving, and specialised craft. The most resilient creatives will be those who adapt their skills and shift their value from execution to higher-level thinking and decision-making. AI Tech Pack Generator (Website) Generate product visuals, technical drawings, multi-view renders, and a complete factory-ready tech pack in minutes from a description. A UX Design Perspective on Improving AI Safety (6 minute read) A lawsuit over a teenager's death after months of conversations with a Character.AI companion bot frames the limits of on-screen disclosures. State laws such as Washington's HB 2225 now mandate repeated non-human disclosure and self-harm protocols, which risk becoming banner blindness. A duty of care is proposed, with public reporting on how often safeguards fail rather than descriptions of perfect guardrails. Thissaway refreshes historic golf resort The Belfry following major expansion (4 minute read) The Belfry Hotel & Resort has unveiled a new brand identity by Thissaway to coincide with major investments in its facilities, including a new conference centre and wellness hub. The rebrand is built around the historical meaning of a belfry-a bell tower that brings people together-which reflects the resort's role as a destination for celebrations, events, and shared experiences. The updated identity features a refined bell symbol, contemporary serif typography, an expanded colour palette, and a flexible system that extends across the resort's spa, club, dining venues, signage, digital channels, and marketing materials.

content: OFF-PREM Ryanair adds Google to its dual-cloud flight plan Gemini gets to juggle crews, forecasts, and maintenance while AWS keeps its seat Ryanair has signed a five-year agreement with Google Cloud covering AI, productivity tools and multi-cloud infrastructure, just weeks after renewing its deal with rival AWS for another five years. The Irish budget airline says it will deploy Google Workspace and Google Cloud services across its 35,000-strong workforce as it pursues a target of 300 million passengers a year by 2034. We asked how much this deal is worth, but Google declined to say and Ryanair did not respond. The rollout includes the Mountain View firm's Gemini Enterprise agentic AI platform, which Ryanair intends to use to automate some decision-making, optimize flight crew logistics, and improve staff productivity. The airline will also use Google DeepMind's AlphaEvolve to refine algorithms and WeatherNext for forecasting and maintenance planning. Ryanair renewed its agreement with AWS for another five years on July 27, making AWS and Google Cloud the two pillars of what the airline itself calls its dual-cloud resilience strategy. Google says the dual-cloud setup will allow critical systems to switch between providers if one suffers an outage, helping keep flight operations, and customer services running. Under the renewed AWS agreement, Ryanair will continue using services including Amazon Quick, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore for workloads ranging from its website to operational planning across a fleet of 647 aircraft. Reg readers may recall that AWS and Google Cloud were touting a jointly developed multi-cloud connectivity service at the end of last year. This links Google's Cross-Cloud Interconnect with AWS Interconnect, allowing customers to set up a private high-speed link between resources they have running on the two cloud platforms. "Ryanair is on an incredible growth journey to 300 million passengers by 2034. To support this growth, we need to ensure we have excellent infrastructure resilience, and our new dual-cloud strategy provides this," commented the airline's CEO, Eddie Wilson. "We are thrilled to be Ryanair's AI transformation partner," stated Maureen Costello, Google Cloud VP for UK, Ireland and Sub-Saharan Africa. "This agreement demonstrates how deploying generative AI at scale - coupled with modern collaboration tools for frontline workers - can help industry leaders scale securely, reduce operational costs, and redefine the travel experience." ®

title: Regal ties its voice AI agents into Five9’s contact center platform

Crucially, data flows both ways: Five9 sends detailed historical call records (campaign, duration, agent) to Regal, ensuring any subsequent contact—human or AI—starts with complete context. author: Duncan Riley
content: Enterprise voice artificial intelligence company Regal Voice Inc. today unveiled an integration with Five9 Inc. that makes its autonomous AI voice agents available to customers of the contact center software provider. Five9 lists the agents in its AI Agent Connect program, a distribution channel for third-party AI vendors. A Five9 call event can now trigger a follow-up from Regal, either a text message or an outbound call placed by an AI agent. Nothing has to be queued by hand. Data runs the other way too. Five9 feeds call records into Regal as calls complete, including the campaign behind each one, how long it lasted and how it ended. The record also shows which agent took the call. Whoever handles the next contact, human or AI, starts with that history. There's a lead routing angle as well. Regal scores contacts for intent through its journey orchestration software, and anything it marks as high intent can go straight into a Five9 outbound campaign without anyone touching it. Regal co-founder and Chief Executive Alex Levin said the pitch is aimed at enterprise contact centers, particularly those in regulated industries, and that the agents are designed to "integrate into existing workflows." Regal started up in New York in 2020. Healthcare, insurance and education are among the industries it sells into, where what a call center rep can say is often tightly scripted. The agents work inbound and outbound calls across sales, support and operations. The company puts its customer base above 200 enterprises. Signals and data from more than 500 million calls feed the software. Regal claims a 99.5% resolution rate without human handoff. Regal has raised $83 million to date, most recently $40 million in October 2024 . The integration lands as Five9 pushes its platform toward agentic software. Five9 sells to more than 3,500 enterprises in more than 140 countries and has been cloud-based since it launched in 2001. Genius AI is its in-house AI layer. Five9 reported its most recent quarter on April 30 , and the stock rose about 18% on the results. Subscription revenue growth picked up for a second quarter running. title: Wolverine on the PS5 made me care about Marvel’s mutant for the first time
teaser: Playing Marvel's Wolverine revealed more than just bloody combat; the character's deep vulnerability unexpectedly endeared him to the writer.
summary: A review of the 'Marvel's Wolverine' demo highlights how much depth exists beyond its gory action. The article, which covered a session at Insomniac Games’ office, details Wolverine's journey rejoining Team X as a reluctant hero with deep emotional barriers. While combat requires chaining attacks to build a Rage meter for devastating powers like Last Stand, the true appeal came during quieter narrative moments in Princess Bar. These scenes underscore Logan's vulnerability and regret. The writer notes that Insomniac succeeded not only in delivering visceral action but also in establishing a meaningful character arc—a necessary feat given Wolverine's relative obscurity compared to Spider-Man. 'Marvel's Wolverine' launches on the PS5 on September 15th.
author: Kallie Plagge
content: Going into my demo of Marvel's Wolverine , I mainly wanted to try out the game's very bloody combat . And it is delightfully bloody. But after two-ish hours of slashing and stabbing (and parrying!) enemies with Wolverine's claws, I left surprised - despite no previous attachment to the character, I was deeply endeared to Logan himself. The demo, which was held at Insomniac Games' office in Burbank, California, started at the beginning of the game. In this story, Wolverine is rejoining the mutant task force Team X after a few years away in order to fight for his fellow mutants. He's a reluctant hero with rocky relationships and little memory of his past - all good ways to onboard a newcomer without having to do a straight-up Wolverine origin story. As Logan relearned how to be Wolverine, I was learning how to be him for the first time. Combat started out a little clunky for me as a result. It's all about chaining attacks and kills to build the Rage meter, which gives you access to stronger and more devastating attacks to end combos with, all while dodging ranged attacks and parrying melee ones. It was a lot to keep track of amid showers of blood from eviscerated enemies. I found myself repeatedly trying to dodge melee attacks rather than parry them, which led to more than a few deaths as I learned the ropes. So maybe it's on me and the difficulty of learning new game mechanics under time pressure, but Wolverine felt far more vulnerable than I expected. This is a character whose nature revolves around being able to take punches. Building up the Rage meter unlocks Last Stand, which lets you get back up from a downed state and go a little berserk for a bit, and that does make him feel feral and dangerous. As do the gruesome finishing moves, most of which involve shredding or impaling enemies in delightfully over-the-top ways. But despite his super-fast healing and adamantium skeleton, Wolverine can die. He's an apex predator in many ways, but he's also a wounded animal lashing out in fear. That's underscored by the original story Insomniac wrote for the game and its characterization of Logan outside of combat. After the bloody opening act, the demo skipped ahead to a quieter sequence in which Logan had to go around Princess Bar and talk to his friends. His relationships here are marked by bitterness, regret, and concern about the barriers Logan has built between himself and the people he cares about. He especially felt like a sad puppy in these conversations, an outcast among outcasts. It was in Princess Bar that I really fell for the character. My last real exposure to Wolverine was 2017's Logan , and while I liked the movie, I didn't have any particular affinity for him one way or another. But after fighting as Wolverine and seeing his lethality, paired with his vulnerabilities in and out of combat, I understood the character in a way I hadn't before. I felt a surge of affection for the man who wants to care and be cared for but is afraid of his capacity to hurt everyone around him. If you're a Wolverine fan, you probably already knew this. But coming off of Insomniac's Spider-Man games, the near-immediate connection I felt after just two-ish hours with this version of him is an important piece of Wolverine 's pitch. Everyone knows Spider-Man, the ever-present hero with hit after hit in theaters pretty much every few years. The Spider-Man games didn't need to sell anyone on being Spider-Man; they needed to sell the fantasy of what it would be like to be him, the one most of us had in our minds already, and Insomniac succeeded on that front . Lots of people know Wolverine, of course, but far fewer people know what the character is truly about compared to a cultural behemoth like Spider-Man . It's a testament to Insomniac's characterization out of the gate - and its scrappy, deadly, but still vulnerable combat - that I came into the demo expecting just some fun, gory mayhem and came out of it wanting to protect Wolverine at all costs. Marvel's Wolverine launches on the PS5 on September 15th. Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates. title: I looked inside an AI generated movie, and the best parts were all human
teaser: Despite being entirely generated by AI, a new film 'Cully Hill Boys' reveals that its strongest elements are rooted in human storytelling and artistic direction.
summary: The article analyzes 'Cully Hill Boys,' an ambitious AI-generated movie from Higgsfield. While the platform showcases advanced generative tools (like Anthropic's Claude for prompts and Seedance 2.5 for video), the reviewer notes that the film's narrative cohesion, pacing, and style are strongly guided by human creatives. Key contributions include a script written by Tim Planagan and the use of likenesses from real public figures: Matt Kiatipis, Mikyle "N3on" Rafiq, and Israel Adesanya. The prompts themselves often mimic signature styles (e.g., 'Guy Ritchie coverage'), indicating that the AI models were trained on human IP. Overall, the film is viewed as a highly polished proof-of-concept highlighting the synergy between cutting-edge AI tech and essential human storytelling craftsmanship.
author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
content: Imagine a trio of bumbling, English lads who fantasize about becoming megastars while knocking back a few pints in a grimy pub somewhere in London. Picture the guys chortling and trying to one-up each other's idealized visions of the future with a series of increasingly glitzy fantasies in which their fame leads to access to groupies and lavish parties on luxurious boats. Imagine these men are actually characters in a film - one filled with hyperkinetic smash cuts to action sequences in which they're fighting or running from armed goons. This movie might be the sort of feature you'd expect from directors like Edgar Wright or Guy Ritchie. But all of this actually comes from Cully Hill Boys , the latest project from the AI filmmaking platform Higgsfield. Cully Hill Boys is one of the few AI movies out this year that comes anywhere near close to looking and feeling like a traditionally produced feature. A large part of the movie's strength is almost certainly rooted in how much Wright and Ritchie's style has been baked into it, and it's not just visual inspiration. In addition to posting Cully Hill Boys online , Higgsfield published many of the prompts that were used to make it. Several of those prompts mention Wright and Ritchie by name, which, along with a script written by a real screenwriter, underlines how the best parts of these films are undeniably taken from actual human artists. Cully Hill Boys tells the story of three struggling rappers from East London whose lives are turned upside down when they accidentally steal a crime lord's money. The project is codirected by Adilet Abish and Aitore Zholdaskali - who also helmed Higgsfield's Hell Grind feature - and is based on a script that was initially written by Tim Planagan before it landed on the Black List screenplay submission service for unproduced projects. After acquiring the script's AI production rights, Higgsfield tapped streamer Mikyle "N3on" Rafiq , basketball content creator Matt Kiatipis , and UFC fighter Israel Adesanya to "star" as its leads. Though none of Cully Hill Boys ' actors shot any scenes on set, each of them signed licensing agreements with Higgsfield for their likenesses to be used in the project. And while Planagan gave Higgsfield the ability to adapt this story using generative AI, he still retains the rights necessary for it to be produced traditionally. Rather than trying to release Cully Hill Boys in theaters, Higgsfield - another service that sells access to various AI models - uploaded the film and most of its constituent prompts online in order to showcase what's possible with its Cinema Studio suite of AI filmmaking tools . The film also functions as a gigantic ad for Higgsfield's newly added Seedance 2.5 functionality, and to highlight new ways that studios can collaborate with digital creators. What's most striking about Cully Hill Boys as you begin to watch it is the way its story moves much in the same way most direct-to-video action / comedies usually do. We're introduced to Cal (Kiatipis), Horace (Rafiq), and Oli (Adesanya) as a trio of longtime friends who just can't figure out how to realize their dreams of becoming well-known musicians. After establishing the boys' interpersonal dynamics, the film zooms out to show us more about who they are individually. Oli's mom insists that he gets a real job, Cal's ex doesn't believe he can be a good father to their daughter, and Horace doesn't have a lot going on outside of being the group's designated driver. Cully Hill Boys establishes all of these details in its first few minutes with a series of scenes that flow together with a tonal and visual smoothness that you seldom see from AI films regardless of their length. Cully Hill Boys' story was crafted by a human with an understanding of proper pacing. Some of that likely boils down to the way that Seedance 2.5 is capable of churning out much longer (about 30 seconds) clips than other video generation models. With films created with AI video models that only generate a few seconds of footage at a time, you can usually see and hear exactly when clips have been stitched together as a way to work around the technology's limitations. There's still some of that in Cully Hill Boys , but many of the project's scenes unfold at a pace that feels much more organic and closer to what you might expect from a traditionally made feature. Watching the movie, I got the sense its plot's general cohesion was a reflection of Zholdaskali and Abish - who led a team of nine other directors, according to Higgsfield - closely following the beats of Planagan's script. Planagan has said that he doesn't use AI tools in his writing process, and it definitely feels like Cully Hill Boys is a stronger film than Hell Grind because its core narrative was crafted by an experienced, human storyteller with an understanding of proper pacing. There's a clear logic to characters' dialog, and the avatars have a passable emotiveness that speaks to how Higgsfield created them using photos and audio clips provided by real people. But when you pay close attention to things like incomprehensible text in books and the way that characters often have a distracting lack of chemistry, it's easy to clock that most of the movie was made by feeding prompts into various generative models. Scrolling through Higgsfield's official Cully Hill Boys page, it's actually fascinating to see how many different iterations of individual shots the film's creative team generated using text prompts. Anthropic's Claude was used to come up with prompts, which were sent to Seedance 2.5 to create video and speech, while ByteDance's Seedream and Google's Nano Banana were used for image and video editing. Per the website, Cully Hill Boys ' creative leads had to split their workflow across different models "because the rules of one job poison the other." That meant, for example, one instance of Claude had to be focused solely on churning out prompts with wording specifically designed to generate workable images while another was dedicated to doing the same for prompts that would eventually become videos clips. Similar to how Cully Hill Boys as a whole feels like an ad for Higgsfield as one of the many AI filmmaking platforms out there, the company's transparency about how the film was made comes across as a way to highlight all of the models it gives its users access to. Reading the text prompts - most of which were in English, while some were in Simplified Chinese - you can see how detailed their descriptions are. But when you compare specific prompts to their corresponding scenes in the full movie, it becomes clear that these models aren't just whipping up impressive shots and camera movements out of thin air. It's evident there's an extra bit of human work guiding this project. More than a few of the prompts related to Cully Hill Boys ' zippier, more action-packed scenes reference elements of Wright and Ritchie's styles of filmmaking. The prompts didn't contain explicit directions to mimic any specific one of Wright or Ritchie films, but they did include asks for "GUY RITCHIE COVERAGE" and "DYNAMIC clip-style (Edgar Wright snap.)" It's not unusual for traditional directors to pay homage by replicating one another's signature filmmaking techniques. But Cully Hill Boys ' is a different sort of beast because its production process seemingly hinges on its underlying AI models having first been trained on Wright and Ritchie's IP in order to understand when they're being asked to generate similar footage. As impressive as Cully Hill Boys is compared to other AI movies, it feels more like a (mostly) polished proof of concept than a project that's ready for the mainstream spotlight. Rafiq, Kiatipis, and Adesanya's fans might get a kick out of seeing their faves in a feature-length production, but this probably isn't something that most moviegoers would be keen to watch. Higgsfield likely understands that reality. Cully Hill Boys ' real value is in its potential to further normalize the idea of AI movies in people's minds. title: This JCB doesn't dig – it does 406 mph
teaser: JCB's hydrogen racer set a world land speed record of 406 mph using advanced engines, proving clean energy can power extreme speeds.
summary: JCB has achieved a major engineering milestone, setting a new world land speed record with its specialized hydrogen-powered racer, the Hydromax. Driven by Wing Commander Andy Green, the vehicle clocked 406.320 mph (653.909 kph) at Utah's Bonneville Salt Flats. The race was officiated by the Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA). The Hydromax is powered by two production-based engines that deliver a combined 1,600 bhp, showcasing JCB's commitment to clean energy. Since starting a £100 million hydrogen engine investment program in 2021, JCB argues that hydrogen is suitable for heavy equipment needing long operation hours. Burning hydrogen produces zero carbon dioxide at the tailpipe, marking a major step in demonstrating sustainable, high-power machinery.
content: OFFBEAT This JCB doesn't dig - it does 406 mph Pair of reworked production-based engines carry the Hydromax into the record books A JCB has set a new world land speed record, passing 406 mph (653 kph) at Utah's Bonneville Salt Flats. The JCB in question isn't a digger or a dumper, but a hydrogen-powered racer known as the JCB Hydromax , driven by retired Royal Air Force fighter pilot Wing Commander Andy Green. JCB's hydrogen-powered Hydromax vehicle JCB It set the record for the fastest a hydrogen-powered internal combustion car has ever travelled, averaging 406.320 mph (653.909 kph) across two runs at the salt flats this week. JCB says the Hydromax is powered by two production-based engines derived from those used in its commercial machinery. The engines are made at JCB's factory in Foston, Derbyshire, and deliver a combined 1,600 bhp. The firm began a £100 million ($135 million) hydrogen engine investment program in 2021, arguing that battery power is practical for smaller machinery but less suited to heavy equipment requiring long operating hours and rapid refueling. It was given permission to sell hydrogen engines by licensing authorities across Europe last year. Another European engineering company, Bosch, is investing in hydrogen power and disclosed some of its plans back in 2023. However, JCB conceds that the two engines in the Hydromax were "extensively rebuilt to suit the demands of breaking the speed record," fitted with spark plugs designed for a Le Mans 24 Hour engine, for example. Burning hydrogen produces no carbon dioxide at the tailpipe, although a combustion engine can still generate nitrogen oxides. JCB estimates that a full record run consumed just over 2 kg (4.4 pounds) of hydrogen and produced 18 liters (about 5 gallons) of water. Beneath the bodywork is a steel-frame chassis similar to that of a conventional racing car, built with a minimal amount of high-strength tubing. The driver sits in a composite monocoque sub-chassis under a drag racing-style steel roll cage. One of the engines is located behind the driver's position and spins the rear wheels, while the other is located in front and drives the front wheels via a front-facing gearbox. Wing Commander Green is no stranger to land speed records. He was at the controls of the ThrustSSC vehicle when it broke the sound barrier on land, and also drove JCB's Dieselmax when it set the world diesel land speed record. JCB Hydromax with Lord Bamford and Andy Green JCB According to JCB, its chairman, Anthony Bamford, led the hydrogen engine project and came up with the idea of a bid for the hydrogen world land speed record. "Twenty years ago we came to Bonneville with JCB Dieselmax and showed what British engineering could do with diesel power. Today we have done it again, this time with engines powered by hydrogen," Bamford said. "It shows hydrogen works, and it works today at the highest level with zero emissions." The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), motorsport's global governing body, officiated the attempt and has confirmed the 653.909 kph ( 406.320 mph) record. ®

title: X open sources its ranking algorithm, letting users see if they’ve been ‘shadowbanned’
teaser: X is opening its core 'For You' algorithm source code, letting users audit the ranking logic behind what they see.
summary: X announced a major push for platform transparency by open-sourcing its core 'For You' algorithm and ranking engine code on GitHub. This significantly expands X’s available codebase, making the underlying parameters—which weight different signals displayed to users—publicly auditable. Additionally, X is rolling out an 'Under the Hood' tool that lets eligible users download JSON stats showing if any labels have been applied to their accounts or posts in a month. These changes aim to address long-standing user concerns regarding algorithmic influence and content distribution fairness, allowing developers even to submit code suggestions for improvement.
author: Sarah Perez
content: X is significantly expanding its open source codebase, which includes the app's "For You" algorithm and its core ranking engine, and adding a feature that will let users see if their account or posts have been impacted by any of its ranking systems, the social network said on Thursday. The company is making the source code for the "For You" timeline, the default feed you see when you open the app, available on GitHub under the Apache v2 license. It's also expanding its previous efforts to open source parts of its codebase to add more detail, including the model configuration, filter, and core ranking system details. That means it includes the parameters used to weight different signals - key to understanding which posts are actually displayed. This also makes the codebase roughly 10 to 15 times larger than it was before. "You'll get the core ranking code that pulls posts and ranks them for any given user and assembles the feed," X's VP of Product Keith Coleman told TechCrunch in an interview ahead of the announcement. "You can see the systems that filter out potentially problematic, rule-violating content...And some of those systems, like the ranker and the score, you can even run yourself outside the company." "This is the kind of thing that I think people will be fairly shocked that we are releasing," he added. In addition to the repository , X is providing tools that will let users see for themselves if and how X's ranking systems have impacted their account or posts. A new transparency tool is rolling out to an "Under the Hood" page in the app's settings, which will let users who have posted 10 or more times over the past month download their aggregate stats as a JSON file. The file will show if any labels have been applied to their account or posts over the past calendar month. Non-technical users can take advantage of this information by dropping it into an LLM of their choice, pointing the AI at X's GitHub repo, and asking for an interpretation. The company notes this tool will initially be available to a test group of accounts at least a year old as a pilot, before rolling out more broadly. Image Credits: X screenshot Ahead of launch, the company previewed its open source codebase to external researchers familiar with recommendation systems, who were able to train and run X's Phoenix scoring system using the open source code. That was a major milestone for X's transparency efforts, Coleman says. From the GitHub repository, developers will be able to submit updates, known as pull requests, which X engineers will consider incorporating into its algorithm. While not all additions will make the cut, Coleman is enthusiastic about the idea. "That would be amazing to have people submitting code that improves the algorithm...I mean, how cool would it be for the X algorithm to be not just visible to the public, but also, like, by the public?," he said. However, a few systems are not included in this release, like those that use Grok to predict whether a post could be violating a rule. This is meant to protect X from bad actors who could use this information to work around the company's rules to flood the network with spam. The changes are meant to address continuing concerns about how X's algorithm influences politics, elections, the spread of misinformation, and more. The platform has been home to political figures and high-profile individuals for years, and is now owned by a trillionaire who helped President Trump get elected. But Twitter had been under attack over its lack of transparency before it was bought by Musk, too. In earlier years, Republicans in Congress alleged that the California-headquartered social network leaned too far left, and claimed the network had "shadowbanned" their posts - meaning their posts were made invisible or undiscoverable without their knowledge. Twitter consistently denied this was the case. "Our dream is that anyone in the public can be able to assess how posts are distributed on the platform, vet that it's a level playing field, and, if they think it's not, critique it so we can keep improving it and addressing it," Coleman said. "That's the whole goal of this: [the code] can be audited; it can be critiqued. We're going to listen, and we want to make the system one that people like and trust, and feel is fair," he said. Though X may be pushing itself to be more transparent around its code and other features, like its crowdsourced fact-checking system, Community Notes, it arguably became less transparent overall under Musk, after becoming a private company again. As it was no longer required to report to the SEC, X was not as forthcoming in other areas, like its user metrics , growth, revenue , or government takedown requests , which are now less frequently reported . Now merged with SpaceX, its monthly active users are once again public. Correction: Included a clarification that X merged with SpaceX and now reports public numbers around user metrics. Coleman also said during the interview that external researchers were about to get "the whole score up and running themselves," but the company clarified that they trained and ran the Phoenix scoring system themselves, but did not get the per-post score.

title: The Corvette Grand Sport X delivers Porsche 911 performance for a fraction of the price
teaser: The 2027 Corvette GSX delivers incredible performance—721 hp for less than half the price of a high-end rival!
summary:
The 2027 Corvette Grand Sport X is a powerful super-hybrid mid-engine sports car, delivering 721 horsepower in an AWD platform that blurs the lines between pure gasoline and electric power. Powered by a stroked V-8 (LS6) with 409 cubic inches, it achieves 520 lb-ft of torque and performance metrics like 0-60 mph in 2.4 seconds.

Crucially, the GSX is positioned as an affordable blast of performance, with a base price ($112,195) far lower than its high-performance counterpart, the ZR1X ($227,395). Its smaller battery (1.9 kWh) isn't focused on range but on absorbing regenerative energy to augment engine output.

The GSX reflects a major industry shift: hybrids are rapidly gaining market share, outselling EVs by nearly three-to-one in America through June (15.4% market share). While some view electric vehicles as the future, the vehicle's hybrid setup uses advanced algorithms to seamlessly blend ICE and EV power, making it competitive with expensive rivals like the McLaren Artura.
author: Lawrence Ulrich
content: My drive of the 2027 Corvette Grand Sport X began under oily black clouds, a torrential weather front releasing its grip on Manhattan - an inauspicious start for any mega-powered sports car. Rain pelted the waterlogged pavement, as I set course for the mountain-man roads of the Catskills, then on to Long Island and New England over three days. Fortunately, this Grand Sport, a name synonymous with value among Corvette fans, was the first of its kind: A 721-horsepower super-hybrid with a brainy, confidence-boosting AWD system. I popped the Corvette into Sport mode, Wet mode be damned. Finding tire grip galore on the Palisades Parkway, I realized the "X" badge on those wide flanks had changed the forecast to "fun." As a track-centric mid-engine sports car, the 2027 Corvette Grand Sport X is hardly representative of mass-market transportation. But the GSX still has something hopeful to say - or shout, with every seismic blast of its new LS6 V-8 engine - about the world's renewed love affair with hybrids. People have always made a statement about who they are, or the person they want to be, through the car they drive or the one they dream of owning. Beetle or BMW, Porsche or pickup, Stingray or Subaru. These choices are more fraught than ever as a zero-sum game emerges between EVs and internal combustion engine cars. You can watch that standoff unfold on YouTube, with drag races between Teslas and seemingly every ICE car since the Model T. When I came of age in Detroit, true sports-car fans scoffed at such reductive straight-line contests, the equivalent of an arm-wrestling match to determine the most gifted athlete. On a broader level, it doesn't have to be this way. Electrified cars like the Grand Sport X can help change the conversation and build common ground on today's scorched earth. The Corvette's sophisticated algorithms bring two often-warring tribes together. There's electric business in the front, and a gasoline party in the back, with no physical connection between the electrified front axle and petroleum-powered rear wheels. Finely coordinated teamwork and integration makes the GSX the latest all-wheel-drive hybrid sports car that feels like an unfair fight against purely gasoline models. GM could use some teamwork on the hybrid front. The company currently has just two gas-electric models. Both are Corvettes. Both use electricity strictly to boost performance, like a hybrid F1 racer, with fuel economy not part of the brief. In America, only hybrids have gained powertrain market share in 2026, with both EVs and pure ICE losing ground. With a record 15.4 percent of the market through June, hybrids are outselling EVs by nearly three to one. Even in China, hybrid sales are growing faster than those of EVs. The Corvette's sophisticated algorithms bring two often-warring tribes together Three companies, Toyota, Hyundai and Honda, now control 90 percen t of this booming US hybrid market. Toyota and Lexus alone sold 600,000 hybrids through June. The windfall has seen Hyundai and Kia post their best overall sales in history, including a 115-percent jump for Kia's growing hybrid lineup. Caught flatfooted after having gone all-in on EVs, GM is racing to bring fuel-saving plug-in hybrids back to its showrooms, supposedly beginning next year. The GSX itself replaces the Corvette E-Ray , Chevrolet's first hybrid sports car. But it's an entirely different animal. The 650-horsepower E-Ray was a versatile grand tourer: fast and fluid, but a bit of a mellow yacht rocker. The GSX was expressly designed as a track assassin, with heightened power, roadholding, braking, and agility. What GM engineers call the "baby ZR1X" adopts its electrified front axle directly from the 1,250-horsepower, 233-mph record setter that I tested at Sonoma Raceway. Most every internal part number is identical. But in keeping with the Grand Sport's reputation as a sweet spot in the Corvette lineup, the GSX coupe's $112,195 base price is less than half that of a ZR1X at $227,395 . For 2027, a non-hybrid, 535-horsepower Grand Sport asks $88,495. That rear-wheel-drive Grand Sport will be more than enough for many buyers. Some want more. So the GSX's 721 horsepower represents a 186-hp bump over a Grand Sport or 2027 Stingray. Add a monumental 655 pound-feet of torque, and the GSX easily tops the 690 horses and 531 pound-feet of a McLaren Artura, a hybrid that starts from around $260,000. As in the ZR1X, the internal bearings in the electric motor were beefed up to handle a higher output of 186 horsepower and 145 pound-feet of torque. Push the GSX's start button, and the engine crackles to life, before settling into a menacing basso idle. Floor the accelerator, and the cabin fills with enough pummeling, martial sound to backdrop a Christopher Nolan epic. The electric motor plays its own whirring part, including a metallic overlay of selected frequencies amplified through the audio system. EV backers may believe silence is golden (sometimes it is) and scoff over ICE fans' unwillingness to give up their thrashing cylinders. What they forget is that an engine's sound offers not just drama and engagement, but critical somatic cues as to how fast you're going, and a car's gear or limits at a given moment. Yes, an EV can digitally imitate those cues. But for now, as with certain music, analog still beats digital among the performance cognoscenti. Yes, an EV can digitally imitate those cues. But for now, as with certain music, analog still beats digital among the performance cognoscenti An optional performance exhaust for $1,995 is a worthy upgrade. Corvette engineers lavished attention on the center-mounted exhaust and its four trumpeting outlets to coax out its most-pleasing harmonic frequencies. Another $2,995 for a front-end lift system is another practical spend, to avoid scraping the low-slung front splitter on every steep driveway. Displacing 409 cubic inches, the stroked V-8 coincidentally harkens to a bygone age of muscle, when Brian Wilson ticked off the Chevrolet Impala SS's technical virtues in the Beach Boys' hit "409." (Hey, it was the '60s). Here in 2026, the LS6 makes that old 409 seem primeval, in tech, power, or efficiency. Pricey forged cylinders can deactivate to save fuel. A lofty 13:1 compression ratio is the stuff of race cars and also contributes to cleaner fuel burn. The engine reduces emissions by 28 percent versus its less-powerful predecessor. The engine's 520 pound-feet of torque sets a high for any naturally aspirated V-8 in production-car history. This overachiever also becomes the standard power plant in a 2027 Stingray, making this "basic" Corvette even more of a sports-car bargain at $73,495. The engine manages a 25-mpg highway rating, impressive for a Stingray that can nip 200 mph. As noted, neither the GSX nor the ZR1X gives a hoot about fuel economy. Their adrenalized performance encourages its pilots to feel the same. The GSX topped out at 22 mpg during my drives. It settled in around 15 mpg, and dipped as low as 11 or 12 mpg during barnstorming runs through the Catskills. Whichever automaker can bring a two-seat, truly mass-produced electric sports car to market - whether Porsche or someone else - energy savings will be an easy win for Team Electric. The Corvette's electric machine is fed by a tiny 1.9-kilowatt-hour battery mounted in the chassis' spine, between driver and passenger. Again, that battery isn't about efficiency or solo electric propulsion. Instead, its cells are designed to absorb regenerative energy like a fast-acting sponge, and spit it back out in rapid bursts. The motor fills any gaps in the engine's output with an unbroken wave of torque, including during paddled upshifts from the eight-speed, dual-clutch automated gearbox. Chevy cites a launch-controlled run to 60 mph in a sparkling 2.4 seconds, and a quarter-mile in 10.4 seconds at 131 mph. I manage 2.6 seconds to 60 mph, even on lumpy backroads in upstate New York. Those official measures are 0.1-seconds quicker than an E-Ray on both counts, and 0.2 seconds quicker than another track-centric Corvette: the mighty Z06 and its Ferrari-esque, flat-crankshaft V-8. As you'd expect, launch starts are less dramatic than in rear-drive Corvettes, all four tires hooking up with a yawn before you're hammered into body-hugging bucket seats. Familiar hardware, including a limited-slip rear differential with selectable Performance Traction Management settings, is retuned for this application. A superlative MagneRide suspension reads the road 1,000 times per second to adjust the viscosity of its magnetic-fluid dampers, and stiffen or soften shocks at individual wheels. The ride is firm but not spine-crunching, especially in Touring mode. Algorithms help dial in electric power for any situation, striving for handling balance and linear power delivery. In familiar tuning disagreements between passionate engineers, every GSX tiebreaker went to the track. As compared to the E-Ray, "we're keeping the edgier scenarios where the car feels more ready to pounce, versus a more-docile character," says Keith Badgley, lead development engineer. The author's gray tester. Image: Lawrence Ulrich Stated simply, electrified front wheels take a major burden off of rear tires, here shod with Michelin Pilot Sport all-season tires in a fat 345/25/ZR21 size. Powerful carbon-ceramic brakes are standard, helping to explain a somewhat eye-opening $23,700 price jump from a standard Grand Sport. Like its ZR1X daddy, the GSX lets me brake deep into corners and jump back on throttle earlier, with fewer worries about the back end getting loose. In the rolling twisties of the Catskills, the GSX felt thrillingly athletic and on-its-toes. Hard-working front wheels palpably yank the 'Vette out of fast corners. Common sense is the only thing that will stop you. The GSX also adopts the ZR1X's specialized performance strategies. Hitting a "Charge +" button summons an Endurance mode, ensuring electrified wheels can deliver a consistent AWD jolt over a full tank of fuel, even during track sessions. A Qualifying mode preps the car for the fastest possible lap. Push-to-pass mode offers the full monty of gasoline and electric power on demand. To keep peace with neighbors, a Stealth mode lets the Corvette roll on electric power alone at speeds up to 50 mph. The energy strategies make it virtually impossible to run the battery below 40 or 50 percent on public roads, no matter how hard you try. Selecting Charge + will also refill the battery over five miles or less of driving, using the gasoline engine and kinetic energy to generate electricity via the motor. Did I mention this Grand Sport makes a great first impression? Rolling into fabled Woodstock, the GSX underscored how the eighth-generation Corvette is (finally) widening its appeal beyond a traditional Boomer, rock n roll audience. I can still quibble with aspects of the C8 design, especially that bluff back end. But the Grand Sports' 3.6-inch-wider chassis, cavernous side air inlets, and forged aluminum wheels add to its exotic supercar vibe. Everywhere I rolled up in the glowering gray GSX, someone would stop in their tracks to offer questions or compliments. And not just car fans, but people who didn't always realize this was a Corvette, but were visibly impressed when they found out. Serious fans will recognize a Grand Sport's traditional hash marks on rear fenders, rendered in classic Admiral Blue on my test car. The Corvette's reworked interior will also win friends. A new auxiliary screen sits just left of the steering wheel, for easier access to launch control and PTM settings. There's an intuitive Google-based infotainment system, graphical performance readouts, and the ingenious camera-based Performance Data Recorder to record and analyze track laps using telemetry software. A removable hardtop remains a signature coupe feature, and a GSX convertible starts from $119,195. My GSX coupe started from $122,845 at its richest 3LT trim level. A schmear of options lifted that to $140,080. By old measures, that's a lot of money for a Corvette. But a Porsche 911 Carrera 4 GTS hybrid, with 189 fewer horsepower, starts from $191,650, and soars past $220,000 with a modest sprinkling of options. And again, the GSX costs roughly half the price of a ZR1X. From the chip-on-shoulder Corvette to Porsche, Ferrari, Lamborghini and McLaren, buyers who might be ambivalent about EVs are warming to this new breed of hybrid sports cars. Their advantages are becoming harder to resist. For any type of car or SUV, I'll argue that the hybrid love affair, rather than being seen as a rejection of EVs, is exactly the opposite. It's a sign that Americans are already willing to meet electrification halfway. The next step becomes that much easier. title: Suno is trying to look more like a real music production tool
teaser: Suno Studio 2.0 adds MIDI support and an AI chatbot that creates custom effects, taking it closer to professional music production tools.
summary:
Suno has released Studio 2.0, significantly upgrading its capabilities to mimic a professional Digital Audio Workstation (DAW). The most crucial update is the addition of MIDI support, allowing users to input played notes or chords as prompts for AI generation, extending melodies, or creating new sections.

The platform also gains automation controls for mixing tracks and integrates an advanced chatbot. This context-aware assistant can automatically enhance vocal tracks by adding professional effects like reverb, compression, or EQ. Furthermore, Suno introduces a suite of simple built-in effects and the ability to create and save custom effects plugins within its Studio environment.
author: Terrence O’Brien
content: Suno is releasing Studio 2.0 with significant upgrades that push it closer to an actual digital audio workstation (DAW), rather than a bare-bones audio editor with generative AI features. The biggest addition is undoubtedly MIDI support. Suno says that MIDI was its most requested feature, and it's basically a prerequisite for any modern DAW. Unfortunately, Suno Studio doesn't appear to support third-party plugins or VSTs yet, so you're stuck using its proprietary built-in synth. That synth appears to be a basic two-oscillator wavetable plugin with three envelopes and four LFOs. The point is less about using your favorite Arturia vintage synth emulation, though, and more about using that MIDI data as a prompt. You can play in some chords, then ask Suno to turn that MIDI into audio, extend a melody, or write a B-part based on what you played. Another standard DAW feature being added in Studio 2.0 is automation. So now you can pan or change the volume of individual tracks across the arrangement. Suno is also adding a chatbot to the Studio interface so you can prompt it for lyrics or a new guitar line. This isn't an isolated generator either, it is tied into the current session and pulls in the musical context of your current project. So you can tell it things like "make this vocal track sound better," and it will add reverb, compression, and EQ. Oh, and yes, Suno Studio now has a suite of simple built-in effects, including distortion, delay, reverb, compression, and EQ. The most interesting feature of the chat interface, however, is the ability to create custom effects plugins. These can be unique reverbs, brickwalled compression, or chorus effects, similar to Polyend's Endless AI guitar pedal. These effects are saved to your account as well, so they can be reused at a later date. Suno Studio 2.0 is a lot more feature-packed than version one, but the beta version of the chat leaves even less to do for the users. In the demo above, Suno's Henry Phipps can be seen cleaning up some flubbed notes and quantizing MIDI, before saying he should be asking the chatbot to do all this for him. He also leaves deciding on a vocal chain up to the AI rather than selecting effects himself. Correction August 13th: This story originally stated Suno's built-in synth had four envelopes instead of four LFOs.

title: Meta adds AI screening to detect WhatsApp scams
teaser: WhatsApp now features AI screening to detect scams, displaying private warnings visible only to the user before they continue chatting.
summary: Meta has integrated an AI screening feature into WhatsApp designed to help users identify potential scam attempts. If the model flags a message as a likely scam, the user receives a private warning within the chat, which is invisible to the recipient. Upon receiving this alert, the user can choose to block, report, or continue the conversation. The system also allows users to manage false positives by marking chats as 'trusted,' thereby removing the warning and preventing future alerts on that specific thread. For continuous improvement, users who mark a chat as trusted can voluntarily opt in to share their last 5 messages with WhatsApp.
author: Stevie Bonifield
content: If the model identifies a message as a likely scam attempt, the user sees a warning in the chat, which is not visible to the other person. From there, the user can decide what to do: block, report, or continue the conversation. If they decide that a warning is incorrectly flagged, the user can mark the chat as trusted, in which case the warning is removed and Scam Alert will not flag that chat again. If a user marks that they trust a chat, they can also opt in to share the last 5 messages received with WhatsApp to help improve the feature's accuracy.

title: Ford’s $28,000 Fathom EV nears production after $2 billion factory overhaul
teaser: Ford bet $2 billion to remake its factory, aiming to produce the affordable Fathom EV starting in 2027 using a radically new assembly process.
summary:
Ford is overhauling its Louisville Assembly Plant to produce the next-generation, electric pickup truck, dubbed Fathom. The company announced prototypes will enter production in Q1 2027, marking a massive shift from gas cars to an all-EV focus. To support this, Ford is investing $5 billion and creating 4,000 new jobs.

The manufacturing process itself has changed entirely; rather than a single conveyor line, Ford employs a three-branched 'assembly tree' system. This radical change utilizes large aluminum unicastings for the front and rear sections, increasing efficiency by up to 15%. Advanced technology is also integrated, such as an early software module flash station using private 5G for quality testing.

The Fathom aims to be affordable at $28,000, following setbacks like losing money on previous EV efforts. The restructuring represents a major attempt to modernize Ford’s operations, echoing its Model T era revolution.
author: Andrew J. Hawkins
content: Ford said today that its next-generation electric vehicle - recently dubbed Fathom - will go into production at the automaker's recently overhauled Louisville Assembly Plant in the first quarter of 2027. The first Fathoms will be prototypes, with Ford's team in Louisville already in the production-level pre-tooling phase at the recently converted facility. Factory workers are working alongside team's at Ford's New Model Product Development Center in Dearborn, Michigan, hand-building the Fathom prototypes - and the same operators who helped design the high-stakes EV will also be involved in its production. The factory is over 70 years old, so Ford had a lot of equipment to get rid of before it could begin the process of converting into an EV plant. Over several weeks, crews physically unbolted and hauled out heavy machinery, dragging thousands of tons of steel out the door. By February, only an empty shell remained. The Fathom, a $28,000 electric pickup truck, will be the first vehicle on Ford's new Universal Electric Vehicle Platform , an innovative new system designed to maximize aerodynamic range while also reducing production costs so Ford can make a profitable vehicle. For over a year, the company has been hyping it as its "Model T moment" that will revolutionize nearly everything at the 123-year-old company. Ford said it converted the plant from one that makes gas cars, like the Escape and the Lincoln Corsair, to an EV only plant in just under a year. In total, Ford is spending $5 billion to create 4,000 new jobs at both the Louisville factory and its BlueOval Battery Park in Michigan. Even the production process will be totally different. Rather than one long conveyor, Ford is using a new assembly tree process that splits the vehicle into three sections - front clip, rear clip, and battery deck - which enables better access so more operators can work on the vehicle at the same time. Ford will use large unicasting to create the front and rear sections, replacing dozens of stamped and welded parts as it currently uses. Ford says it can speed up the production process by up to 15 percent by using the assembly tree. To illustrate how much more efficient this new process will be, Ford cites this example: One example of that efficiency in action is the software module flash station, a first for a Ford assembly plant, which ensures vehicles have the latest software prior to module installation. Previously, this software flash happened after the vehicle was built, and if issues were detected, updates took 10 minutes per vehicle. With private 5G in the plant, operators can perform quality tests like these as a vehicle rolls down the assembly tree Ford is banking on this new streamlined process, as well as its core competency of building a high-volume of vehicles, to make the Fathom's retail price a reality. To be sure, Ford hasn't had the best of luck when it comes to EVs. The company lost over $5 billion on EVs and software in 2024 , and another $4.8 billion in 2025. The company was forced to cancel the F-150 Lightning, a truck once heralded as the most important EV ever made.

title: OpenAI hires new CRO as executive shake-up continues
teaser: OpenAI replaced CRO Denise Dresser and bought back $7B in shares, signaling significant internal shake-ups and strategic pivots ahead of a possible IPO.
summary: Amid an executive shake-up marked by several departures (including CRO Denise Dresser, replaced by Dali Rajic), OpenAI is refocusing on enterprise deployment and measurable business impact. The company's strategic pivots are visible through major financial moves, including the purchase of $7 billion in employee shares, valuing the firm at $852 billion. While filing confidentially with the SEC for an IPO, this tender offer suggests a potential delay or complex timing for public listing.
